CHAPTER 19

## Pediatric Growth and Development

## NOTES

## DEVELOPMENTAL ASSESSMENT: APPROACH

- Watchful observation
- $ Developmental: play and exploration of the exam room
- $ Relational: interactions between the child and family
- $ Biological
- $ Cultural

## Suspect a Developmental Delay?

- Categorize and document delays.
- $ Physical
- $ Cognitive
- $ Language
- $ Social-emotional
- $ Self-care
- Refer the child for a formal developmental assessment.

## Formal Developmental Assessment

- Includes formal tests, parent questionnaires, child observation
- Determines the appropriateness of early interventions
- $ Counseling/family support
- $ Educational adaptations
- $ OT/PT/Speech

## Classifications by Age

- Premature infant: born before 37 weeks' gestation
- $ Early term: 37.0-38.6 weeks
- $ Late term: ≥39.0 weeks
- Newborn: Birth to 28 days
- Infant: 1-12 months
- Toddler: 15-35 months
- Preschool: 3-5 years
- School age: 6-10 years
- Adolescent: 11-21 years

## Newborn Exam: Growth and Development

- Gross motor
- Fine motor
- Visual behavior
- Personal-social
- Language
- Reflexes
- Fontanels

## Newborn: Motor Development

- Gross motor
- $ Lifts head
- $ Equal movements in all extremities
- Fine motor
- $ None to speak of

## QUESTION #1

A full-term newborn infant exhibits asymmetrical movement of the left upper extremity. Clavicular crepitus is present. Which of the following might have contributed to this?

1. Macrosomia
2. Group B Strep infection in birthing parent
3. A CN VI disorder
4. Vitamin D deficiency in birthing parent

## Newborn: Personal-Social

- Regards another's face
- Human eyes are bright and shiny, so newborns should track caregivers' eyes

## Newborn: Language

- Cry: communication tool for hunger, pain, attention, cold
- High-pitched cry can indicate neurologic disorder
- $ Example: "Cri-du-chat"

## QUESTION #4

A 1-week-old male newborn does not have a red reflex in his right eye. Which of the following might this indicate?

1. Pupillary insufficiency
2. Strabismus

4. Congenital glaucoma

## Newborns: Visual Behavior

- Red reflex should be present bilaterally at birth.
- Absent red reflex
- $ Consider congenital cataracts
- $ Retinoblastoma
- Vision is about 20/200 to 20/400

## Newborn: Ocular Discharge

- Purulent ocular discharge
- $ Gonococcus
- $ Chlamydia
- $ Herpes
- Chemical conjunctivitis
- Erythromycin ointment used to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum (ON) caused by gonorrhea

Courtesy of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

In a normally developed term infant, which of the following fontanels is normally open at birth?

1. Anterior only
2. Posterior only
3. Anterior and posterior
4. Anterior always; posterior sometimes

## QUESTION #6

When assessing an infant, you notice that they do not have a startle reflex (arms extend from body with sudden head drop). This may indicate that this child has:

1. hearing loss.
2. central nervous system damage.
3. a visual defect.
4. developmental delays.

## Newborns: Ears

- Low-set ears
- $ Renal agenesis
- $ Chromosomal abnormalities
- Assess gross hearing by observing for startle response
- Auditory brainstem response
- $ Hearing screening at birth
- $ Repeat if negative

## Newborn: Ears

- Significant bilateral hearing loss
- $ 0.1-0.3% of newborns
- $ 2-4% of NICU graduates
- AAP recommends: universal hearing screening by 1 month
- $ Goal is to detect hearing loss before age 3 months
- $ Interventions by 6 months

## QUESTION #7

An infant weighs 7 pounds at birth. What would you expect this infant to weigh by age 1 year?

1. 16 pounds
2. 19 pounds
3. 21 pounds
4. 24 pounds

## Growth in Infants

- Newborns lose 5-7% of their birth weight in the first days.
- Infant weight changes rapidly!
- $ Return to birth weight by age 2 weeks
- $ Gains 1 ounce/day
- $ Doubles birth weight by 4-6 months
- $ Triples birth weight by 1 year
- Head circumference increases 0.5 inches per month
- Lengthens 1 inch/month

## 2-Month-Old: Motor Skills

- Grasps rattle if placed in hand
- Able to lift head 45° and has some control when torso held upright

<!-- image -->

© MartinPrescott/E+/Getty Images

<!-- image -->

## 2-Month-Old: Personal-Social Development

- Infant should:
- $ Focus on face
- $ Smile responsively
- $ Seem happy to see caregiver
- $ Calm when spoken to

## 2-Month-Old: Language Development

- Vocalizes sounds that reflect happiness or being upset
- Makes short cooing sounds

<!-- image -->

## QUESTION #8

A 6-week-old infant has an open posterior fontanel. What does the NP tell the parents?

1. This fontanel will stay open until about age 9 to 18 months.
2. The posterior fontanel should close by 3 months.
3. The baby should be referred to Neurology.
4. The posterior fontanel usually closes by 8 weeks.

## 2-Month-Old: Visual Behavior

- Intense eye contact
- Vertical and circular tracking
- Interested in mobiles
- Disconjugate gaze
- Red reflex present bilaterally

## 4-Month-Old: Fontanels

- Anterior open
- Posterior closed

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

NOTES

## NOTES 4-Month-Old: Motor Skills

- Head up to 90°
- No head lag when pulled upright
- Sits with head control
- Follows with eyes past midline
- Grasps rattle

## 4-Month-Old: Personal-Social Development

- Smiles spontaneously
- Chuckles
- Makes sounds to get caregiver attention

## 4-Month-Old: Language & Vision

## Vision

- Intense eye contact
- Vertical and circular tracking
- Interested in mobiles
- Grasps toward hanging objects
- Disconjugate gaze

## Language

- Vocalizes
- Oohs and aahs
- Laughs
- Turns head toward sound of voice

## QUESTION #9

An infant just learned to push himself up on all four limbs. How old is the infant likely to be?

1. 1 month
2. 2 months
3. 4 months
4. 6 months

<!-- image -->

## 6-Month-Old: Development

- Lots of changes!
- $ First teeth emerge
- $ Introduction of solid foods: "Food before 1 is just for fun!"
- $ Introduce a cup
- $ Can try water with meals
- Anterior fontanel remains open

## 6-Month-Old: Motor Skills

- Bears weight on legs
- Lifts chest using arm support
- Rolls over
- Sits with support, maybe unsupported

## 6-Month-Old: Language & Personal-Social Development

Language

- Squeals
- Turns toward rattling sound
- Takes turn making/mimicking sounds
- Blows "raspberries"

## Personal-social development

- Works to obtain toy
- Smiles often and interacts with caregiver
- Knows familiar people
- Looks at self in mirror

## 6-Month-Old: Reflexes

- Parachute reflex appears.
- $ Infant extends arms, hands, and fingers when suspended prone and lowered quickly toward table.
- $ Never disappears
- Many reflexes have disappeared by 6 months.
- $ Moro, stepping, rooting, palmar grasp, Galant, tonic neck

## QUESTION #10

At what age should eye alignment occur?

1. Within the first 2 months of life
2. By 3 months of age
3. By 6 months of age
4. By 12 months of age

## 6-Month-Old: Visual Behavior

- Conjugate gaze
- Watches own hands
- Reaches toward and grasps hanging objects
- Color vision develops by 5 months

## Vision Screening in Children

- Once a child develops conjugate gaze (older than 6 months), they should be screened for strabismus.
- $ Strabismus: deviation of one eye due to oculomotor weakness ➔ amblyopia
- $ Amblyopia: loss of vision in one eye
- When the two eyes don't focus on the same object, the brain ignores information from one of the eyes.

## QUESTION #11

Which of the following tests is used to identify strabismus?

1. Red reflex
2. Snellen chart
3. Cover-uncover test
4. Visual tracking

## Strabismus Screening in Children

- Cover-uncover test to assess for strabismus
- Start at 6 months through 3 years

## 9-Month-Old: Growth

- Growth is about as rapid as at 6 months
- Length increases: 0.5 inches per month
- Weight increases: 3-4 ounces per week
- Head circumference increases: 0.25 inches per month

<!-- image -->

## 9-Month-Old: Motor Skills

- Pulls to sit
- No head lag
- Sits without support
- Crawls/scoots
- Holds to stand
- Looks for yarn
- Rakes raisin using fingers
- Passes a cube

## 9-Month-Old: Personal-Social Development

- Feeds self with hand
- Stranger anxiety develops
- $ Shy, clingy, fearful

## 9-Month-Old: Language

- Turns toward voice
- Uses single syllables

## 12-Month-Old

## Growth:

- Length increases: 3 inches per year
- Weight increases: 4.5-6.5 pounds annually
- Weight should have tripled by this time
- Head circumference increases: 1 inch annually

## Personal-social development

- Plays pat-a-cake

<!-- image -->

## 12-Month-Old: Motor Skills

- Pulls to stand, may take a few steps
- "Cruises" using furniture
- Bangs blocks together
- Thumb-finger/pincer grasp
- Stands 2 seconds
- Feeds self and drinks from cup easily
- Looks when name is called
- Reacts when you leave
- Plays peek-a-boo
- Imitates speech sounds
- Lifts hands to be picked up

<!-- image -->

© Ole.CNX/Shutterstock

<!-- image -->

NOTES

## NOTES 12-Month-Old: Language & Vision

Language

- Dada, mama
- Combines syllables
- Waves "bye-bye"
- Understand "no"

## Vision

- Looks through window
- Recognizes people
- Recognizes pictures

## 15- to 24-Month-Old: Development

- What to assess
- $ Gross/fine motor skills
- $ Psychosocial emotional: no longer assess personal-social
- $ Language
- $ Reflexes: plantar disappears at 12-24 months
- $ Fontanels: anterior open but okay if closed
- $ Visual acuity: conjugate gaze

## 15- to 24-Month-Old: Development

|           | Gross Motor                                       | Fine Motor                                                | Psychosocial Emotional                                             | Language                                  |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| 15 months | · Stands alone · Stoops and recovers · Walks well | · Puts block in cup                                       | · Indicates wants · Waves bye-bye                                  | · Jabbers · "dada" "mama" · Says one word |
| 18 months | · Walks backward                                  | · Scribbles · Builds tower of two cubes                   | · Plays ball with examiner · Imitates activities · Drinks from cup | · Says two to three words                 |
| 24 months | · Runs · Walks up steps · Kicks ball forward      | · Dumps raisin, demonstrated · Builds tower of four cubes | · Uses spoon/fork · Removes garments · Feeds doll                  | · Says six words · Points to picture      |

## QUESTION #12

The caregiver of a 15-month-old child reports that the child is not yet walking independently, rarely responds to their name, and produces only a few sounds such as "ba" or "da." What is the most appropriate evaluation of the child's developmental status?

1. Reassure the caregiver that children develop at their own pace.
2. Recommend increasing social interaction at home with reassessment at 18 months.
3. Refer the child to early intervention services for a comprehensive evaluation.
4. Order neuroimaging studies to rule out structural brain abnormalities.

## Preschooler Development: Ages 3 to 5 Years

- What to assess
- $ Gross/fine motor skills
- $ Psychosocial emotional
- $ Language
- $ Visual acuity (conjugate gaze)

|         | Gross Motor                                                                                                                           | Fine Motor                                                                            | Psychosocial Emotional                                                                                     |
|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 years | Jumps up Throws ball overhand Rides a tricycle                                                                                        | Builds tower of six cubes, uses scissors, copies circle                               | Puts on clothing, brushes teeth with help                                                                  |
| 4 years | Jumps a short distance, balances 2 seconds on each foot, catches a bouncing ball, throws ball underhand, walks down steps alternately | Copies vertical line, builds tower of eight cubes, wriggles thumbs, dresses/undresses | Washes/dries hands, names friend, puts on t-shirt                                                          |
| 5 years | Hops, balances 3 seconds on each foot, skips, walks backward toe to heel, can somersault                                              | Draws person in three parts, copies +, triangle, square, prints own name              | Dresses self, plays board games, brushes teeth without help, imaginary friend, shows affection, group play |

## Preschooler Development: Ages 3 to 5 Years

|         | Language                                                                                                                                   | Visual Acuity   |
|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| 3 years | Combines words, IDs one picture, names six body parts, points to four pictures, speech half understandable                                 | Vision: 20/50   |
| 4 years | Knows two actions, two adjectives, names one color, uses two objects, counts one block, names four pictures                                | Vision: 20/40   |
| 5 years | Knows four actions, uses three objects, ALL speech understandable, understands four prepositions, names four colors, 1,500-word vocabulary | Vision: 20/30   |

## Middle Childhood Development: Ages 6 to 10 Years

- What to assess
- $ Gross/fine motor skills
- $ Psychosocial emotional
- $ Language
- $ Cognitive
- $ Moral development
- $ Physical development

NOTES

## NOTES Middle Childhood Development: Ages 6 to 10 Years

|          | Gross Motor                                                                            | Fine Motor                                                                   | Psychosocial Emotional                                                                                                              |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 6 years  | Balances on each foot 6 seconds, heel-to-toe walking, precise and deliberate movements | Picks longer line from choices, copies square, draws person in six parts     | Prepares cereal, enthusiastic about surroundings, identifies left and right, some understanding of death and dying, wants to please |
| 8 years  | Increased physical strength and endurance                                              | Well developed hand-eye coordination, good finger control                    | Develops close circle of same- gender friends, enjoys group activities, peer pressure, mood swings, impatient                       |
| 10 years | Capable of demanding motor and endurance tasks (bicycling)                             | Handles tools well, manual dexterity developed, capable of drawing in detail | Dislike of opposite gender, generally dependable, same- gender friends                                                              |

## Middle Childhood Development: Ages 6 to 10 Years

|          | Language                                                                                     | Cognitive                                                                                                                                           |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 6 years  | Defines five to seven words, knows three adjectives, counts five blocks, knows two opposites | Easily disappointed and frustrated, reads well, vocabulary of 10,000-14,000 words, uses appropriate verb tense, words, and sentence structure       |
| 8 years  | Almost able to converse at adult level, enjoys reading, understands how opposites work       | Wants to understand how and why things work, clear, logical thinking skills, exhibits preference for certain subjects and activities                |
| 10 years | Continues to improve reading, comprehension, writing skills                                  | Good at memorizing, recalling info but not understanding it, eager to learn new skills, capable of concentrating & resuming task after interruption |

## Middle Childhood Development: Ages 6 to 10 Years

|          | Moral Development                                                                                            | Physical Development                                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 6 years  | Rules are absolute, values consequences over intentions with a focus on avoiding punishment.                 | Visual acuity: 20/20, tonsils & adenoids reach largest size, retina fully developed, eustachian tube becomes longer and more slanted, completely toilet trained, gains strength and coordination |
| 8 years  | Rules can be changed, begin to understand intentions, Internalize sense of right & wrong, fairness & justice | Alveolar development complete, rapid maturation of endocrine system, long bones grow                                                                                                             |
| 10 years | Right from wrong based on society/peer's perception of the action, develops empathy & understanding          | Continues with physical growth, girls may begin breast development                                                                                                                               |

## Adolescent Development: Ages 11 to 21 Years

- What to assess:
- $ Psychosocial emotional development
- $ Cognitive
- $ Moral development
- $ Physical/sexual development (male and female)

## Adolescent Development: Ages 11 to 21 Years

|                                | Psychosocial Emotional                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Early adolescence 11-14 years  | Concern over body image, looks, clothes, conflicts between high expectations and lack of confidence, eating problems may develop, peers are source for standards and models, interest in opposite gender, strives to be accepted, preoccupied with self, erratic and inconsistent behavior                                          |
| Middle adolescence 15-17 years | More interest in opposite gender, sex drive emerges, increased independence from parents, prefers spending time with friends, prone to feeling sad or depressed, concerned with attractiveness, conflicts over parental controls and independence, struggle for acceptance of greater authority, questions about sexual orientation |
| Late adolescence 18-21 years   | Sets goals and follows through, involved in community issues, greater emotional stability, acceptance of social institutions and cultural traditions, greater concern for others                                                                                                                                                    |

## Adolescent Development: Ages 11 to 21 Years

|                                | Cognitive                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Early adolescence 11-14 years  | Strong desire to learn useful things, able to use logic and debate others, usually focuses on the present, prefers active learning over passive learning, independent critical thinking develops from arguing                            |
| Middle adolescence 15-17 years | Deeper capacity for caring and sharing, develops more intimate relationships, intellectual sophistication and creativity, increased concern with peace, poverty, environment                                                             |
| Late adolescence 18-21 years   | Articulates thoughts, expresses ideas, higher level of concern for future, concerned about role in life, ability to make independent decisions, defined work habits, pride in work, more developed sense of humor, ability to compromise |

## Adolescent Development: Ages 11 to 21 Years

|                                | Moral Development                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Early adolescence 11-14 years  | Tests rules and limits, begins to understand potential consequences of future behaviors, develops ideals, selects role models, experimentation: drugs, sex, EtOH, and tobacco |
| Middle adolescence 15-17 years | Questions social norms, understands concepts of good and evil                                                                                                                 |
| Late adolescence 18-21 years   | Able to delay gratification, self-reliant, personal dignity, self-regulation of self- esteem, continued interest in moral reasoning                                           |

NOTES

## NOTES Adolescent Development: Ages 11 to 21 Years

|                                | Male Physical Development                                                                                                                   | Female Physical Development                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Early adolescence 11-14 years  | Rapid height gains (10 cm/year), ravenous appetite, metabolism fluctuations, extreme restlessness, body proportions similar to adult        | Increased coordination and strength, rapid vertical growth, body proportions similar to adult                                                                                                    |
| Middle adolescence 15-17 years | Nearing completion of vertical growth, acne and body odor prevalent, periods of excessive physical activity followed by periods of lethargy | Nearing completion of vertical growth, height completion ceases 2-2.5 years after menarche, acne and body odor prevalent, periods of excessive physical activity followed by periods of lethargy |
| Late adolescence 18-21 years   | Continues to gain weight, muscle mass, and body hair                                                                                        | Fully developed                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## QUESTION #13

An 8-year-old child is caught lying about taking a toy from a classmate's backpack. When asked why they took it, the child replies, "Because I really wanted it, and no one saw me." Based on Kohlberg stages of moral development, which level best evaluates the child's current stage of moral reasoning?

1. Preconventional level-Stage 1: obedience and punishment orientation
2. Preconventional level-Stage 2: individualism and exchange (self-interest)
3. Conventional level-Stage 3: good interpersonal relationships
4. Postconventional level-Stage 5: social contract and individual rights

Kohlberg stages of moral development

## SPORTS PREPARTICIPATION EVALUATION (PPE)

## Sports PPE

- Most children participate in a sport at some point during their school years.
- Perform 4-6 weeks before participation.
- Provide age-appropriate anticipatory guidance.

## Visit Goals

- Preparticipation evaluations (PPE) have several goals: primary goal is safe participation!
- $ Recognize children who might experience lifethreatening complications from participation.
- $ Identify children with medical problems that must be addressed to allow for safe participation.
- $ Intervene and rehab children with history of musculoskeletal problems.
- $ Optimize health conditions that may be exacerbated by activity.

## Components

- Standard evaluation forms have been endorsed by several organizations, including American Academy of Pediatrics.
- $ School-specific forms
- $ Organization-specific form
- Medical history should be completed by parents and child together if possible.

## Medical History: Cardiac Concerns

- Past/current cardiac conditions
- Syncope and heat-related events
- Symptoms
- $ Fatigue
- $ Shortness of breath
- $ Chest pain
- Abnormal cardiac testing

## Physical Exam: Cardiovascular

- Vital signs: look for elevated blood pressure, height, weight
- $ Body composition is measured for wrestling if low weight.
- Auscultation: murmurs, gallops, rubs
- Femoral pulses: should be equal (if unequal, consider coarctation of the aorta) REFER!!
- Assess medical history:
- $ Immunizations
- $ Medications
- $ Menstrual history
- $ Weight changes
- Family history
- $ Heart disease
- $ Unexplained sudden death
- $ Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
- $ Inheritable arrhythmias

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## NOTES

## NOTES Neuro/Musculoskeletal Considerations

- Pay special attention to the spine, shoulder blades, iliac crest, tibial tuberosities.
- PE:
- $ Muscle atrophy or injury
- $ Passive and active ROM
- $ Previous injuries
- $ Previous concussion

## Physical Exam Considerations

- Eyes
- $ Refer if visual acuity is worse than 20/40.
- Skin
- $ Infectious diseases: participation, only if lesions can be covered or are noncontagious
- Lymph nodes
- $ If enlarged, consider further workup
- Respiratory
- $ Listen for wheezing and consider EIB workup.
- Abdomen
- $ Organomegaly?
- Genitourinary
- $ Protective cup
- Especially if history of cryptorchidism

## Participation Recommendations

- Options for clearance
- Full clearance
- $ With or without recommendations for primary care follow-up
- Clearance with limitations
- Exclusion from participation

headers: 6 years
Rules are absolute, values consequences over intentions with a focus on avoiding punishment.
Visual acuity: 20/20, tonsils & adenoids reach largest size, retina fully developed, eustachian tube becomes longer and more slanted, completely toilet trained, gains strength and coordination
rows: Rules can be changed, begin to understand intentions, Internalize sense of right & wrong, fairness & justice
Alveolar development complete, rapid maturation of endocrine system, long bones grow
Right from wrong based on society/peer's perception of the action, develops empathy & understanding
Continues with physical growth, girls may begin breast development

headers: Early adolescence 11-14 years

Concern over body image, looks, clothes, conflicts between high expectations and lack of confidence, eating problems may develop, peers are source for standards and models, interest in opposite gender, strives to be accepted, preoccupied with self, erratic and inconsistent behavior
rows: More interest in opposite gender, sex drive emerges, increased independence from parents, prefers spending time with friends, prone to feeling sad or depressed, concerned with attractiveness, conflicts over parental controls and independence, struggle for acceptance of greater authority, questions about sexual orientation
Sets goals and follows through, involved in community issues, greater emotional stability, acceptance of social institutions and cultural traditions, greater concern for others

headers: Early adolescence 11-14 years

Strong desire to learn useful things, able to use logic and debate others, usually focuses on the present, prefers active learning over passive learning, independent critical thinking develops from arguing
rows: Deeper capacity for caring and sharing, develops more intimate relationships, intellectual sophistication and creativity, increased concern with peace, poverty, environment

Articulates thoughts, expresses ideas, higher level of concern for future, concerned about role in life, ability to make independent decisions, defined work habits, pride in work, more developed sense of humor, ability to compromise

headers: Early adolescence 11-14 years
Tests rules and limits, begins to understand potential consequences of future behaviors, develops ideals, selects role models, experimentation: drugs, sex, EtOH, and tobacco
rows: Questions social norms, understands concepts of good and evil
Able to delay gratification, self-reliant, personal dignity, self-regulation of self- esteem, continued interest in moral reasoning

headers: Early adolescence 11-14 years
Rapid height gains (10 cm/year), ravenous appetite, metabolism fluctuations, extreme restlessness, body proportions similar to adult
Increased coordination and strength, rapid vertical growth, body proportions similar to adult
rows: Nearing completion of vertical growth, acne and body odor prevalent, periods of excessive physical activity followed by periods of lethargy
Nearing completion of vertical growth, height completion ceases 2-2.5 years after menarche, acne and body odor prevalent, periods of excessive physical activity followed by periods of lethargy
